description: An empty-string batting hand is a real group value: those players stay in every step and are compared with the other empty-hand players.

c.request: For each player in the postseason batting data (matched to `player` on `player_id`), take their average postseason doubles per record, ignoring missing values, along with their batting hand. Divide it by the overall average of these per-player averages to get a relative index. Then show how far each player's index sits above the average index for their batting hand. Give the top 10 players by that gap, largest first (missing last), with player id, batting hand, average doubles, index, and the gap, unrounded. An empty-string batting hand is a real group value: those players stay in every step and are compared with the other empty-hand players.
c.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        b.player_id,
        p.bats,
        AVG(CAST(b.double AS REAL)) AS average_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS b
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = b.player_id
    GROUP BY b.player_id, p.bats
),
indexed AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        average_doubles,
        average_doubles / AVG(average_doubles) OVER () AS index_value
    FROM player_averages
)
SELECT
    player_id,
    bats,
    average_doubles,
    index_value,
    index_value - AVG(index_value) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap
FROM indexed
ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

b.request: For each player with postseason batting records, join `batting_postseason` to `player` by `player_id` and calculate that player’s average `double` across records, ignoring NULL values. Divide each player’s average by the overall average of those per-player averages to get an index, then subtract the average index for players with the same batting hand to get the gap. Treat an empty-string batting hand as a real group value throughout. Return the 10 players with the largest gaps, sorting NULL gaps last, with `player_id`, batting hand, average doubles, index, and gap, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.player_id,
        p.bats,
        AVG(bp.double) AS average_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS bp
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
player_indices AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        average_doubles,
        average_doubles / AVG(average_doubles) OVER () AS index_value
    FROM player_averages
)
SELECT
    player_id,
    bats,
    average_doubles,
    index_value AS "index",
    index_value - AVG(index_value) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap
FROM player_indices
ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

a.request: Matching postseason batting records to players on `player_id`, work out each player's average postseason doubles per record (ignoring missing values), grouped by player and batting hand (`player.bats`). Turn that into a relative index by dividing it by the overall average of these per-player averages. Then compare each player's index with the average index of players who have the same batting hand. List the 10 players whose index is furthest above their batting-hand average. Show the player id, batting hand, average doubles, index, and index minus the hand average, sorted by that difference from highest to lowest (missing values last), unrounded. Treat an empty batting hand as its own batting-hand group. Players with a missing (NULL) batting hand still count toward the overall average but are not listed.
a.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT p.player_id,
           p.bats,
           AVG(bp.double) AS average_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS bp
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
player_indices AS (
    SELECT player_id,
           bats,
           average_doubles,
           average_doubles / NULLIF(AVG(average_doubles) OVER (), 0) AS index_value
    FROM player_averages
),
hand_averages AS (
    SELECT bats,
           AVG(index_value) AS hand_average_index
    FROM player_indices
    WHERE bats IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY bats
)
SELECT pi.player_id,
       pi.bats,
       pi.average_doubles,
       pi.index_value AS index,
       pi.index_value - ha.hand_average_index AS index_minus_hand_average
FROM player_indices AS pi
JOIN hand_averages AS ha
  ON pi.bats = ha.bats OR (pi.bats = '' AND ha.bats = '')
WHERE pi.bats IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY index_minus_hand_average DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

d.request: For each player in the postseason batting data matched to `player` by `player_id`, calculate their average postseason doubles per record, ignoring missing values. Treat an empty-string batting hand as a real group value and include those players throughout. Divide each player’s average by the overall average of the per-player averages to get a relative index. For each player, calculate the difference between their index and the average index for their batting-hand group. Show the 10 players with the largest gaps first, with missing gaps last. Include player ID, batting hand, average doubles, index, and gap, without rounding.
d.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.player_id,
        p.bats,
        AVG(bp.double) AS average_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS bp
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
player_indices AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        average_doubles,
        average_doubles / AVG(average_doubles) OVER () AS idx
    FROM player_averages
),
player_gaps AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        average_doubles,
        idx,
        idx - AVG(idx) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap
    FROM player_indices
)
SELECT player_id, bats, average_doubles, idx, gap
FROM player_gaps
ORDER BY CASE WHEN gap IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, gap DESC
LIMIT 10;
